stories.headline: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.title: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.summary: If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone over the Bay of Bengal in quick succession during ongoing North-East monsoon season after severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu late last month
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bay of Bengal is once again emerging as a potential breeding ground for a cyclone, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) flagging a fresh formation alert over its central parts by Monday evening.

A low-pressure area that lay over the south-east Bay on Friday is forecast to intensify into a depression by Sunday before rapidly strengthening in two successive stages over exceptionally warm ocean waters.
If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone in quick succession during the ongoing North-East monsoon season.

Severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu had struck the Andhra Pradesh coast in rapid succession late last month, even as a developing El Niño over the equatorial eastern Pacific presented a seemingly contradictory backdrop to the unusually active storm season.

With the Bay continuing to host an active MJO pulse and oceanic conditions remaining favourable, the coming days will be crucial in determining whether the developing ‘low’ graduates into another powerful cyclone.
The immediate focus will be on how quickly it organises, how long it retains access to favourable atmospheric conditions, and, eventually, which stretch of the eastern seaboard it threatens.

The emerging system is drawing support from an active Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), which has gained considerable amplitude over the Bay before preparing to resume its eastward journey towards the South China Sea.
The MJO is an eastward-moving pulse of enhanced cloud formation, thunderstorms and atmospheric circulation along the tropics.

When its active phase passes over a tropical ocean basin, it can create conditions conducive to cyclone formation by encouraging rising air, strengthening low-level atmospheric rotation and reducing the disruptive influence of vertical wind shear, or changes in wind speed and direction with height.
The MJO is therefore favouring cyclogenesis over both the Bay and the Arabian Sea, although this does not necessarily imply that El Niño is contributing to the process.
El Niño operates on a much larger canvas, altering atmospheric circulation, wind patterns, moisture availability and the distribution of tropical convection across ocean basins.
Its influence on cyclone formation is not uniformly favourable.

stories.headline: Can the turmoil over Indian Olympic body’s election affect it’s 2036 bid?
stories.title: Can the turmoil over Indian Olympic body’s election affect it’s 2036 bid?
stories.summary: Can the turmoil over Indian Olympic body’s election affect it’s 2036 bid?
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The bad publicity over upcoming Indian Olympic Association (IOA) elections, with it’s current president PT Usha in the eye of the storm, could not have been worse timed for the country’s Olympics bid aspirations.

It hasn’t escaped the eyes of the International Olympic Committee (IOC), which has sent a strongly worded letter to the Indian Olympic body to set their house in order ahead of the country’s presentation for 2036 Olympics bid on 26th November.

An Indian delegation is set to make a presentation to the IOC’s Future Host Commission as part of the country’s bid to host the 2036 Games, with the likes of Nita Ambani (India’s representative in IOA) and Usha, along with officials from the Union and Gujarat governments.
They are supposed to showcase India’s case with Ahmedabad proposed as the host city.

However, the status of former sprint queen Usha - in the wake of her not being able to secure a nomination among the top four women’s Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) ahead of the elections makes her presence in the delegation somewhat untenable.

What’s more, Usha’s surprise nomination from the Ice Hockey Federation of India to contest the IOA elections has now been challenged by advocate Atul Kumar - who has filed a formal objection with returning officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava, challenging her inclusion in the electoral roll.
The decision of the legendary athlete to remain in part of the fray for a tilt at the second term raised enough eyebrows, but many feel it’s more a ‘posturing’ rather than anything else.

She had shot a letter to the IOC top brass earlier this complaining of foul play in the online voting for SOM polls, while she minced no words in an interview with The Tribune where she asked for a scrutiny of the votes polled for long jump ace Anju Bobby George – a fellow Malayali.
Usha had finished fifth in the women’s category with 40 votes behind Anju (53), Rani Rampal (50), Dola Banerjee (45) and Saina Nehwal (43).

While such a result is entirely possible, what raised fears of external influence was that the SOM elections were preceded by the withdrawal of 13 candidates – eight men and five women – from the contest for eight places in the General Assembly.
Several athletes subsequently alleged that their withdrawals were not voluntary.
Ashwini Nachappa, a former sprinter and contemporary of Usha, claimed in an interview that she had been asked to pull out under external pressure.

stories.headline: Amit Shah's Pune visit and why BJP wants NCP merger despite Supriya Sule's rejection
stories.title: Amit Shah's Pune visit and why BJP wants NCP merger despite Supriya Sule's rejection
stories.summary: Amit Shah's Pune visit and why BJP wants NCP merger despite Supriya Sule's rejection
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The proposed NCP merger has stalled over leadership differences, with Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar reportedly opposing Sharad Pawar taking charge of the reunited party, while Supriya Sule has declared the merger chapter closed.

The proposed merger of the two Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions appears to have hit a roadblock over the question of leadership, even as the BJP continues to weigh its political and parliamentary calculations around a possible reunion.

While leaders from both factions had reportedly explored the possibility of bringing the two sides together under Sharad Pawar's leadership, Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth Pawar are understood to have reservations about the arrangement.
The leadership dispute has prevented the negotiations from reaching a consensus.

Meanwhile, NCP (SP) working president and MP Supriya Sule has sought to put an end to speculation surrounding the merger and the possibility of her party joining the NDA, declaring that the merger chapter ended with the death of her brother, Ajit Pawar.
The developments have assumed added significance ahead of Union Home Minister Amit Shah's Pune visit on November 15 and 16.
Shah is scheduled to attend a Pune Zilla Parishad programme where a statue of late Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar will be unveiled.
Sources indicate that Shah could also hold discussions with Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar during the visit.

Interestingly, the time allotted for the programme has reportedly been increased from 20 minutes to 40 minutes, triggering speculation about the BJP's political calculations surrounding the possible merger.
Addressing a press conference on Saturday, Supriya Sule categorically denied that her party was discussing a merger with the Ajit Pawar faction or considering joining the NDA.
She maintained that the discussions about bringing the two factions together had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive and that his death had changed the situation completely.
"I am tired of these merger discussions.
